This study evaluates maternal urine hyperglycosylated hCG (H-hCG) levels in pregnancies with Down syndrome. Samples were tested at 10-19 weeks gestation (within 24 weeks). The study used stored maternal urine samples from 349 singleton pregnancies including 45 with Down syndrome, with chromosomal verification as reference standard.

This study evaluates urine beta-core fragment (a metabolite of hCG) as part of a screening algorithm for Down syndrome. The study measured maternal urine beta-core fragment levels prospectively before genetic amniocentesis in 1360 singleton pregnancies, 21 with fetal Down syndrome. Gestational age was midtrimester (within 24 weeks), with chromosomal verification via amniocentesis as reference standard.

This study evaluates both urine free beta hCG and urine beta core as potential screening markers for Down syndrome. Urine samples from 29 cases of Down syndrome, three cases of trisomy 18, and 400 control pregnancies were analyzed. Results were corrected for urine concentration using creatinine. Chromosomal verification served as reference standard.

This prospective study evaluated urine beta-core fragment measurements as a screening test for Down syndrome pregnancies. Fresh urine samples were assayed continuously for 726 pregnancies over 9 months, with 13 Down syndrome cases confirmed by karyotype. Samples were collected at 12-24 weeks gestation.

This study measured maternal urinary beta-core hCG and creatinine at 11-14 weeks gestation in 26 aneuploidies (including 9 trisomy 21 cases) and 198 normal singleton pregnancies. While it found urinary beta-core hCG less discriminating for Down syndrome at 11-14 weeks than later in pregnancy, it still evaluates maternal urine testing for Down syndrome within the specified gestational window.

Samples collected at genetic amniocentesis (mean 16.2 weeks gestation). Reference standard was chromosomal verification via amniocentesis. Meets selection criteria: includes maternal urine tests, within 24 weeks gestation, for Down's syndrome, with chromosomal verification.

Study evaluates a new triple screen test combining urine analytes (beta-core fragment of hCG and total urine estriol) with serum AFP for Down syndrome screening in second trimester. Prospective study with 10 Down syndrome cases and 346 normals. Reference standard was chromosomal verification via genetic amniocentesis. Meets selection criteria: maternal urine tests, within 24 weeks gestation, for Down's syndrome, with reference standard.

Study evaluates multiple urinary analytes (beta-core fragment of hCG and total urinary estriol) combined with nuchal thickness and maternal age for Down syndrome screening. Prospective study in women undergoing genetic amniocentesis at midtrimester (15-24 weeks). Reference standard was chromosomal verification via amniocentesis. Meets selection criteria: maternal urine tests, up to 24 weeks gestation, for Down's syndrome, with chromosomal verification.

Study evaluates sialic acid-deficient invasive trophoblast antigen (sd-ITA), a urinary variant, for gestational Down syndrome screening. Urine samples collected from 16th to 18th week of gestation from 10 patients with trisomy 21 fetuses and 10 normal karyotype pregnancies. Reference standard was karyotype analysis. Meets selection criteria: maternal urine test, within 24 weeks gestation, for Down's syndrome, with chromosomal verification.
